title: CET-6 Section A Simulation — Campus Rooftop Vertical Farm Pilot

dialogue.display_text: Hi Maya, thanks for dropping by. I just finished reviewing your proposal for the campus rooftop vertical farm, and the sustainability committee is genuinely impressed with your ambition.
dialogue.spoken_text: Hi Maya, thanks for dropping by. I just finished reviewing your proposal for the campus rooftop vertical farm, and the sustainability committee is genuinely impressed with your ambition.

dialogue.display_text: Thanks, Professor Miller! We spent months mapping out how hydroponic racks could supply fresh greens to the main dining hall and cut food transport emissions by 35%. Initially, everyone assumed securing the $18,000 equipment grant would be our biggest hurdle. Actually, once the administration saw our energy projections, they approved the funding right away. What's holding us back now is getting structural clearance for the old library roof.
dialogue.spoken_text: Thanks, Professor Miller! We spent months mapping out how hydroponic racks could supply fresh greens to the main dining hall and cut food transport emissions by thirty-five percent. Initially, everyone assumed securing the eighteen thousand dollars equipment grant would be our biggest hurdle. Actually, ... once the administration saw our energy projections, they approved the funding right away. What's holding us back now is getting structural clearance for the old library roof.

dialogue.display_text: That makes sense. The library was built back in 1978, and saturated soil plus heavy water tanks add tremendous weight. Have the campus facilities engineers inspected the site yet?
dialogue.spoken_text: That makes sense. The library was built back in nineteen seventy-eight, and saturated soil plus heavy water tanks add tremendous weight. Have the campus facilities engineers inspected the site yet?

dialogue.display_text: They ran a preliminary assessment last Tuesday. At first, we thought we could install automated climate sensors and high-output LED panels across the entire east wing. Well, the thing is, the engineers warned that concentrated weight in one section could stress the aging steel beams. Instead, they recommended spreading lightweight modular units evenly along the perimeter walls, which keeps the load well within safety limits.
dialogue.spoken_text: They ran a preliminary assessment last Tuesday. At first, we thought we could install automated climate sensors and high-output L E D panels across the entire east wing. Well, ... the thing is, the engineers warned that concentrated weight in one section could stress the aging steel beams. Instead, they recommended spreading lightweight modular units evenly along the perimeter walls, which keeps the load well within safety limits.

dialogue.display_text: Smart adjustment. That also solves your maintenance access issue. Still, running a year-round operation takes consistent labor, and student volunteers usually disappear right around midterm and final exams.
dialogue.spoken_text: Smart adjustment. That also solves your maintenance access issue. Still, running a year-round operation takes consistent labor, and student volunteers usually disappear right around midterm and final exams.

dialogue.display_text: We actually anticipated that exact problem after interviewing clubs at two neighboring universities. Many campus farms fail because they rely solely on unpaid student volunteers who burn out by November. Surprisingly, our biggest breakthrough came from partnering with the Agricultural Science department. They agreed to integrate daily crop monitoring into their introductory lab course, meaning around 40 freshmen will earn practical course credit for tending the system every week.
dialogue.spoken_text: We actually anticipated that exact problem after interviewing clubs at two neighboring universities. Surprisingly, ... our biggest breakthrough came from partnering with the Agricultural Science department. They agreed to integrate daily crop monitoring into their introductory lab course, meaning around forty freshmen will earn practical course credit for tending the system every week.

dialogue.display_text: Tying it directly to academic credit is brilliant—it guarantees steady staffing without draining your budget. So what is your immediate next step before construction can officially kick off in spring?
dialogue.spoken_text: Tying it directly to academic credit is brilliant, ... it guarantees steady staffing without draining your budget. So what is your immediate next step before construction can officially kick off in spring?

dialogue.display_text: Before ordering any modular trays, we still need final sign-off from the campus fire marshal regarding emergency walkway widths. What really matters right now is submitting the revised blueprints by Friday afternoon so our vendor can lock in the winter discount rate before prices go up in January.

dialogue.display_text: Send those updated drawings to my inbox tonight, and I will personally walk them over to the facilities office tomorrow morning.
dialogue.spoken_text: Send those updated drawings to my inbox tonight, and I will personally walk them over to the facilities office tomorrow morning.

questions.spoken_text: Question one. What is currently preventing Maya's team from moving forward with the project?

options.A: Applying for an eighteen-thousand-dollar equipment grant.
options.B: Reducing food transportation emissions for the dining hall.
options.C: Verifying whether the building can safely support the facility.
options.D: Calculating accurate energy projections for the administration.

options.C: Reinforcing the aging steel beams with heavier water tanks.
options.D: Replacing high-output L E D panels to save electrical power.
